subject: Consistent colour coding across multiple trees, possible?

messages.author: 8260f639bf0e9772
messages.subject: Consistent colour coding across multiple trees, possible?
parts:
Hi,

Is there a way to colour code tip/branch labels across multiple trees but have the colours consistent for groups?

I have followed the tutorial here and I can get my branches and tip labels coloured nicely using the groupOTU function but they are given whatever the standard colour set is from ggtree/ggplot2 in a set order.

I have lists that are automatically created from a table with taxonomic IDs, so for example two different trees might produce the lists below:

tree_list_1 <- list(ascomycota=c("A", "B", "C"), basidiomycota=c("F", "G", "H"), blastocladiomycota="M", mucoromycotina=c("L", "K", "I", "J"))

tree_list_2 <- list(ascomycota=c("A", "B", "C"), basidiomycota=c("F", "G", "H"), mucoromycotina=c("L", "K", "I", "J")

The colours are then:
1) red, yellow, light-green, dark-green
2) red, yellow, light-green

But the problem is, because tree list 2 does not have any blastocladiomycota in it, mucormycotina is light-green instead of dark-green. How can I get them to be the same, without creating empty groups which I don't want to have in the legend...?

messages.author: 8260f639bf0e9772
messages.subject: Re: Consistent colour coding across multiple trees, possible?
parts:
Attaching a working example:

For example, in the output from the script below: "basidiomycota" are coloured green in tree 1 and blue in tree 2. I would like it to be consistent across n (I have 40+) trees for each taxonomic group - so e.g. basidiomycota always "blue", ascomycota always "green" etc...

library("ape", lib.loc="~/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/3.3")
library("ggplot2", lib.loc="/usr/local/lib/R/site-library")
library("ggtree", lib.loc="~/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/3.3")

tree1 <- rtree(10)
tree2 <- rtree(10)

tree1_tax <- list(ascomycota=c("t1", "t2", "t3"), basidiomycota=c("t4", "t5", "t6"), blastocladiomycota=c("t7","t8"), mucoromycotina=c("t9", "t10"))
tree2_tax <- list(ascomycota=c("t1", "t2", "t3"), basidiomycota=c("t4", "t5", "t6"), mucoromycotina=c("t7", "t8", "t9", "t10"))

tree1_groups <- groupOTU(tree1, tree1_tax, overlap='abandon')
tree2_groups <- groupOTU(tree2, tree2_tax, overlap='abandon')

tree1_colour <- ggtree(tree1_groups, aes(color=group, linetype=group)) + geom_tiplab() + theme(legend.position="right")
pdf(width = 20, height = 12)
print(tree1_colour)                                
dev.off()

tree2_colour <- ggtree(tree2_groups, aes(color=group, linetype=group)) + geom_tiplab() + theme(legend.position="right")
pdf(width = 20, height = 12)
print(tree2_colour)                                
dev.off()

messages.author: 65135aac151a06a7
messages.subject: Re: Consistent colour coding across multiple trees, possible?
parts:
Using the scale_color_manual() you can manually set the colors. There is also a scale_linetype_manual if you want, but I didn't bother to include it.

library(ape)
library(ggtree)

tree1 <- rtree(5)
tree2 <- rtree(5)

#make three groups we will make "a" blue, "b" green, and "c" red"
tree1_tax <- list(a=c("t1"), b=c("t2", "t3"), c=c("t4","t5"))
#now we condense "b" and "c", which will become red
tree2_tax <- list(a=c("t1"), b=c("t2", "t3", "t4", "t5"))

#now make the groups
tree1_groups <- groupOTU(tree1, tree1_tax)
tree2_groups <- groupOTU(tree2, tree2_tax)

#using the scale_color_manual, we can setup the color groups manually
tree1_test <- ggtree(tree1_groups, aes(color=group)) + scale_color_manual(values=c("blue", "green","red")) + theme(legend.position="right") + geom_tiplab()
tree2_test <- ggtree(tree2_groups, aes(color=group)) + scale_color_manual(values=c("blue","red"))               + theme(legend.position="right") + geom_tiplab()
                   
plot(tree1_test)
plot(tree2_test)

messages.author: 8260f639bf0e9772
messages.subject: Re: Consistent colour coding across multiple trees, possible?
parts:
Hi Ben,

Thanks, I think I see what you are doing but it doesn't really work in the way that I was hoping, perhaps I didn't explain well enough.

In your example; tree1 group "b" is green, and in tree2 suddenly it is "red" when it should be green - I know I can just change the 'colour manual' option from 'green' to 'red' but if I have to set this manually for each tree it will take some time, I was hoping for a more automated way of pushing colour to the leafs.

For example: I always want group "b" to be a set colour, regardless of any tree that I throw at the script, and that means the trees could have groups like this:

tree 1: a, b, c, d
tree 2: a, b, c
tree 3: c, d, e
tree 4: b, c, d
tree 5: a, c, d, e, f

Also a group between the trees might not include the same sampling of taxa but will always be consistent to their taxonomic origin.

Hmm, perhaps I can assign colour names within a list matching against a group of taxonomic names and then place a subset of that matched against the list generated from the tree as a list in the scale_color_manual....!

Best, 

Guy
